item.title: Interpret a trial of quiet-table signs
item.summary: A café owner describes how signs changed behaviour without changing the layout.
item.transcript_text: We put quiet-table cards near the wall. I assumed people would see them as an invitation to work alone. A few regulars did. Others thought we had reserved the tables for staff. We changed the words to ask customers to keep conversations low. Groups began using them, and some moved their chairs into the aisle to talk to friends at the next table. Noise readings fell, but crossing the room became harder. Next month we'll try quieter tables in a separate corner, so the arrangement does some of the work. The trial helped me see how quickly a sign changes what a table means to people. A quieter room is only part of what we were trying to achieve.

questions.prompt: What surprised the owner about the original cards?
options: Nobody saw any cards by the wall
People read the same cards as different instructions
The cards raised the noise level on their own
Staff claimed the labels were unreadable
questions.explanation: Some people understood a quiet invitation and others inferred a staff reservation.

questions.prompt: What did the revised wording change?
options: Groups started using the marked tables
People used the wall only to read signs
Customers left chairs outside the café
Every visitor sat alone
questions.explanation: Groups were willing to use the tables after the label changed.
